settlement.description: One payment-application join record, embedded and owned by the invoice. This is the classic accounting pattern of applying payments/refunds against an invoice: amounts here are always positive and kind alone carries direction, so there is no mirrored list on billing.payment or billing.refund to keep in sync -- the invoice is the only place this relationship is recorded.

amount.description: The portion of the referenced payment or refund applied to THIS invoice -- not necessarily that payment's or refund's full amount. One payment may be split across multiple invoices; one invoice may be settled by multiple payments (split tender). Always positive regardless of kind; kind alone carries whether this portion increases or decreases what's owed. Never zero -- a zero-amount settlement records nothing and should simply be omitted.

id.description: The consumer's own key for the corresponding billing.payment or billing.refund record (whichever kind names), used to look up full detail -- method, processor references, timing -- in the consumer's own system.

kind.description: Which side of the ledger this settlement entry represents. payment increases amountPaid; refund decreases it -- kind carries the direction, so amount itself is always positive.

occurredAt.description: When this settlement was applied, RFC 3339. May differ from the referenced payment/refund's own occurredAt if application to this invoice was recorded later.

description: An accounts-receivable document: embedded line items (snapshotted, see commerce.line-item), a totals block, and a settlements[] ledger recording which payments and refunds have been applied against it. number is human/legal (often gapless by jurisdiction requirement) and is not this schema's identity -- there is no id property; consumers key invoices in their own systems. Every monetary amount in this document, including inside line items and settlements, is assumed to share one currency; this schema cannot cross-check that.

$kind.description: Optional self-identifier (cf. GraphQL __typename). Omit when the enclosing schema already names the role -- a value held under a property literally named invoice is unambiguously an invoice without needing $kind. Include only when this object might appear untyped outside its normal context.

amountDue.description: DERIVED cache, not authoritative: amountDue = total minus amountPaid. When both this field and settlements/total are present, recompute from those rather than trusting a stale cached value; amountDue exists so consumers can read a ready-made outstanding balance without recomputing it every time. Non-negative -- in an overpayment scenario treat amountDue as 0 and track the credit balance separately (e.g. metadata, or a future credit-note schema); this field does not represent a negative amount owed.

amountPaid.description: DERIVED cache, not authoritative: amountPaid = sum of settlements[kind=payment].amount minus sum of settlements[kind=refund].amount. When both this field and settlements are present, settlements is the source of truth; amountPaid exists so consumers can read a ready-made total without recomputing it from settlements every time. Non-negative via the sibling properties/amount/minimum.

billingAddress.description: Address associated with billing for this invoice. No shippingAddress here -- delivery detail belongs to the order this invoice may reference (orderId), not the invoice itself; a consumer needing invoice-level shipping detail has metadata as the escape hatch.

customerId.description: Opaque id of the customer being invoiced, keyed in the consumer's own system.

discountTotal.description: Invoice-level discount applied on top of subtotal, distinct from any per-row discountAmount already reflected in each line item's own amount. Optional -- see total's description for the full identity and sign convention. Non-negative via the sibling properties/amount/minimum, composed alongside the $ref.

externalReferences.description: Links to corresponding records in foreign systems, e.g. Stripe or Shopify -- see external-reference for shape and validation. Replaces ad-hoc *Id fields scattered across schemas with one uniform array.

issuedAt.description: When the invoice was issued to the customer, RFC 3339.

lineItems.description: The priced rows that make up this invoice. At least one is required -- an invoice with zero line items has nothing to bill for.

metadata.description: Freeform escape hatch for consumer-specific data this schema doesn't model. Deliberately non-interoperable -- a private extension zone, not part of the typed interop surface. Recommend reverse-DNS-style keys (e.g. "com.example.internalId") when multiple parties write to it.

number.description: Human-facing, often legally significant invoice number -- many VAT and other tax jurisdictions require these to be gapless sequences. Distinct from the consumer's own system key: this schema has no id property, so number is display/legal, not lookup.

orderId.description: Opaque id of the commerce.order this invoice bills for, keyed in the consumer's own system. billing may reference commerce; the reverse never happens -- package dependency direction is acyclic.

settlements.description: Payment-application history for this invoice: which payments and refunds have been applied, and how much of each was applied here. See the settlement definition in $defs for the shape and rationale. Record a settlement entry only for payments/refunds that have SUCCEEDED -- pending or failed money movement must not enter settlement math, or two producers computing amountPaid/amountDue from the same settlements array will diverge on what happened. Optional -- an unpaid or externally-tracked invoice may have none. When present alongside amountPaid/amountDue, settlements is the source of truth.

status.description: Lifecycle state of the invoice. Absent means draft -- the safe default: an imported or partially-migrated invoice with no recorded status must never be silently treated as open/collectible.

subtotal.description: Sum of line item amounts before invoice-level discount and tax adjustments. Optional -- see total's description for the full identity and sign convention. Non-negative via the sibling properties/amount/minimum, composed alongside the $ref.

taxTotal.description: Total tax for the invoice. Optional -- see total's description for the full identity and sign convention. Non-negative via the sibling properties/amount/minimum, composed alongside the $ref.

total.description: The invoice's grand total, authoritative regardless of whether the optional component totals are present: total = subtotal minus discountTotal plus taxTotal. Shipping charged on an invoice is modeled as its own line-item row, not a separate total -- there is deliberately no shippingTotal here (unlike commerce.order); delivery detail belongs to the order, and an invoice billing for shipping does so as a line item like any other charge. This schema cannot enforce that arithmetic -- consumers compute it, and total is the source of truth for billing even if the components are absent or don't sum to it exactly. Non-negative via the sibling properties/amount/minimum, composed alongside the $ref.
